metaDescription: Five cordless screwdrivers under $30 compared on torque, battery and torque settings, with advice on what a pen or stick driver cannot do that a drill can.
expertTake: The Amazon Basics by SKIL 4V stick screwdriver is the best all-rounder because it publishes real torque numbers and has three torque settings. The SKIL SD561801 is the plainest and cheapest way into the SKIL system, and the Circuit Sensor version adds a useful live-wire detector. The AFNZTME gives you the most torque on paper and the most bits. A cordless screwdriver is for light assembly: if you drive deck screws or build furniture daily, buy a drill instead.
introParagraphs: A cordless screwdriver is a small battery tool that turns a bit with a few inches of torque, enough to drive screws in furniture, electronics covers and outlet plates. It is a convenience tool, not a power tool in the drilling sense, and it sits well below a drill in torque.

This guide explains what torque, battery and chuck design mean at this size, which compromises are harmless and which ones strip screws or leave you stuck. Our top picks sit above, and the reviews below cover the ownership details a box does not mention.

products.name: Amazon Basics by SKIL 4V Cordless Stick Screwdriver
products.description:
This stick screwdriver is a trimmed SKIL design sold under the Amazon Basics label. Its 4V lithium cell is built in and charges over USB-C, so you can top it up from a power bank or a phone charger. Maker figures put it at up to 300 RPM and up to 22 inch-pounds of torque, which is a believable number for a tool this size.

Three torque settings let you pick a lower clutch level for small screws in plastic and electronics, so the driver stops before the head strips. Compared with the AFNZTME's 3.5 N.m claim, about 31 inch-pounds, the Amazon Basics unit gives up some peak force in return for clearer, lower specs and a clutch you can use. A built-in LED lights the screw in a dark cabinet.

Ownership is easy because there is nothing to replace. The built-in cell is the limit, since there is no spare to swap in, but a 2,000 mAh cell at 4V lasts through an afternoon of light assembly. Charge it before a project, not during, and keep the bits in the case so they do not walk away.
products.bestFor: Furniture builders and renters who want a safe, clutch-equipped screwdriver for light assembly.
pros: Three torque settings protect small screws
USB-C charging from any power source
LED lights dark cabinets
Published torque figure you can compare
cons: Too weak for long wood screws

products.name: SKIL SD561801 4V Cordless Screwdriver
products.description:
The SD561801 is the basic SKIL stick driver. It has a two-finger trigger, a collar that flips between forward and reverse, and a USB charging cable. The design keeps the body slim so it fits into tight spots, such as the inside of a cabinet or a narrow shelf bracket.

It has no torque clutch, which is the main difference from the Amazon Basics unit. Without a clutch the driver keeps turning until the motor stalls, and on a small screw in soft wood the head can strip. In exchange it is the plainer tool and often the lowest cost of the SKIL family.

The nine bits and holder cover Phillips, slotted and some hex tips, which is enough for flat-pack furniture. For ownership, keep the bits in the holder, charge it before you start, and use it in short bursts so it does not run flat. If you want a clutch, pick the Amazon Basics model instead.
products.bestFor: People who want the plainest, cheapest SKIL-built driver for flat-pack furniture.
pros: Slim body fits tight spaces
Two-finger trigger is easy to control
USB charging cable included
Nine bits cover common screw heads

products.name: SKIL 4V Cordless Screwdriver with Circuit Sensor
products.description:
The Circuit Sensor model adds a feature that other screwdrivers lack: it detects live current in outlets, switches and fixtures. Holding the tip near a live conductor makes the tool flag it, so you get an extra warning before you unscrew a switch plate or a light fixture. It is a convenience, not a substitute for turning off the breaker and testing the circuit.

Next to the basic SD561801, you pay for that sensor. The core driver is the same, with a 4V battery, a forward and reverse collar and nine bits. Against the Amazon Basics unit, it gives up the three torque settings but keeps a USB charge.

The sensor is the reason to buy this version, and the reason to be careful. A non-contact sensor detects only energized conductors close to the tip, and it can miss a wire behind a wall. Treat it as an alert and still verify with a proper tester. For general assembly it behaves like the other SKIL drivers.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who swap switch plates, outlet covers and fixtures.
pros: Circuit Sensor warns of live current
Slim stick shape for tight spots
USB charge works from a power bank
Forward and reverse collar
cons: Sensor is not a replacement for a tester

products.name: AFNZTME 3.6V Cordless Electric Screwdriver Kit
products.description:
The AFNZTME is the high-spec option in this price class. A 3.6V, 1,500 mAh battery drives a motor rated at 3.5 N.m, or about 31 inch-pounds, which is roughly 40 percent more than the 22 inch-pounds on the Amazon Basics driver. The handle swings between an in-line stick position and a pistol grip, so it works in cabinets and on open panels.

The kit includes 46 bits, which cover Phillips, slotted, Torx and hex tips and a few drill bits for wood and plastic. More bits do not make a better tool, but they spare you a trip to the hardware store when you meet a security screw. The torque figure is a maker claim, so treat it as a peak value and not a working one.

The trade is brand support. Replacement batteries and parts for a small brand are hard to find, and the cell is the part most likely to age out. If you want a project tool with plenty of bits and decent grunt, it is a good choice, but check the return window.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists who want a pistol-grip option and a large bit set in one kit.
pros: Highest listed torque in the group
Handle converts from stick to pistol
46 bits cover many screw types
Includes drill bits for plastic and wood
cons: Brand support and spare parts are thin
Torque figure is a maker claim

products.name: LMQ Mini 30-in-1 Electric Screwdriver Kit
products.description:
The LMQ is a different tool from the stick drivers: a pen-shaped precision screwdriver for electronics, glasses, toys and small appliances. Its 24 magnetic S2 steel bits cover the tiny Phillips, Torx and pentalobe sizes found on phones and laptops. Three LEDs light the work area, which helps when a screw sits deep inside a case.

At this size torque is small, which is the point: you want enough force to run a tiny screw and not enough to snap it. Compared with the Amazon Basics driver at 22 inch-pounds, the LMQ is much gentler, and that is why it suits electronics repair and not furniture. It will not drive wood screws.

The ownership detail to watch is bit quality. S2 steel is a harder tool steel than the chrome vanadium in cheap sets, but it is brittle, so do not use it as a pry bar. A bit that rounds off on a screw head is a sign the bit, not the tool, is worn, and swapping it costs far less than a new driver. Keep the bits sorted in the case and store the tool away from magnets that attract stray steel.
products.bestFor: Electronics and small-appliance repair where torque control matters more than power.
pros: Pen shape gives fine control
24 magnetic bits cover small fasteners
Three LEDs light the work
Light enough for long sessions
cons: Far too weak for wood screws
Small bits are easy to lose

buyingCriteria.explanation: Torque is the twisting force, and at this size the useful range is about 10 to 35 inch-pounds. The Amazon Basics driver claims up to 22 and the AFNZTME about 31. A lower figure protects small screws, and a higher one drives longer screws into soft wood. Match it to the screws you drive: a 1-inch screw into particle board needs only a modest figure, while a 2-inch screw into pine will stall a 22 inch-pound driver and make you finish by hand. If you hit that wall often, the next step up is a 12V drill, not a stronger screwdriver.

A clutch slips at a set torque so the head does not strip. The Amazon Basics driver has three settings, while the SD561801 and Circuit Sensor models have none. If you drive many small screws in plastic or particle board, a clutch pays for itself in saved screws. Without one, the habit that saves you is to stop the trigger early and finish the last turn by hand, which is slow but reliable.

A 4V lithium cell charged by USB is convenient and slow to age. A built-in cell, like the Amazon Basics 2,000 mAh, cannot be swapped. If you assemble all weekend, choose a larger cell like the AFNZTME's 1,500 mAh at 3.6V or plan to charge between jobs. A cell that takes a few hours to refill on USB is fine for a weekend, and annoying only when you forget to plug it in the night before.

A stick shape fits tight spots, a pistol grip gives more leverage, and a pen shape gives precision. The AFNZTME converts between stick and pistol. The LMQ is a pen for electronics. Choose by the job you do most, because a convertible handle that you never use is a feature you paid for.
Bits are consumables and the box count is marketing. A set of 9 good bits beats 46 soft ones. S2 steel bits like the LMQ's hold shape better but snap under side load.

An LED helps in dark cabinets. The Circuit Sensor warns of live current, which is a useful extra, not a replacement for a tester. Likewise a built-in LED is worth having only if it sits close to the bit and does not cast a shadow from your hand.

specDecoder.meaning: The nominal voltage of the lithium cell. At this size voltage does not predict power much because the gearbox changes the torque.
specDecoder.watchFor: A higher number on a cheaper tool is not a mark of better quality.

specDecoder.meaning: The twisting force at the chuck. 1 N.m is about 8.85 inch-pounds. The AFNZTME's 3.5 N.m is about 31 inch-pounds.
specDecoder.watchFor: Makers often print stall torque, which is higher than working torque.

specDecoder.meaning: Battery capacity. A 2,000 mAh cell holds more charge than 1,500 mAh at the same voltage.
specDecoder.watchFor: Comparing mAh across different voltages is misleading, so convert to watt-hours.

specDecoder.meaning: Speed with no load. The Amazon Basics driver is rated up to 300 RPM.
specDecoder.watchFor: Low RPM is normal for a screwdriver and a feature, not a flaw.

specDecoder.meaning: A feature that detects electric current near the tip so you do not touch live wiring.
specDecoder.watchFor: It detects only nearby live conductors, so it is a warning, not a guarantee.

cards.label: Stick
cards.text: A straight body for most assembly work, which fits tight spots. The Amazon Basics, SD561801 and Circuit Sensor models are sticks.

cards.label: Pen and pistol
cards.text: A pen suits small electronics, and a pistol grip gives leverage. The LMQ is a pen, and the AFNZTME is a convertible stick and pistol.

howToChoose.note: Choose a stick for furniture and a pen for electronics.

howToChoose.subheading: For Outlet and Switch Plates Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A slim body, a slotted bit set and a warning for live current. Always turn off the breaker first.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SKIL Circuit Sensor adds the live-current alert, and the Amazon Basics driver adds a clutch to avoid cracking plastic plates. Use a proper voltage tester in either case.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You drive more than light screws. A cordless drill is the real upgrade from any of these tools.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You assemble a few pieces of furniture a year. The SD561801 or LMQ is plenty.

maintenance.why: A mostly charged cell lasts longer, and these tools have no spare battery.
Metal dust and grease make bits slip.
A cell kept full or empty ages faster.
Loose bits are lost and mixed sizes strip screws.
A sticky forward/reverse collar can slip mid-screw.

faq.q: Can a cordless screwdriver replace a drill?
faq.a: No. A screwdriver has torque in the tens of inch-pounds, while a drill has hundreds. It handles light assembly but cannot drill larger holes or drive long screws.

faq.q: How much torque do I need?
faq.a: For flat-pack furniture 15 to 25 inch-pounds is enough. For wood screws over 1 inch you need a drill.
Yes, with a normal USB adapter. Do not leave the tool charging for days.

faq.q: What does the Circuit Sensor do?
faq.a: It beeps or lights when the tip is near a live conductor. It is a warning, and a proper tester is still the safe way to check.

faq.q: Why are there so many bits in the kits?
faq.a: More bits make the kit look better value, but only a few sizes get used. Check which tips you need.

The motor and gearbox usually outlast the battery. A small lithium cell is good for a few hundred charges, which is years of occasional use, but the cell is built in on several of these models and cannot be replaced cheaply. Think of the tool as a roughly five-year item and keep the receipt for returns.
